title: A gym's join code can be found by trying codes, and then anyone can join that gym's member app
what: A gym's join code is 6 characters made only of 0-9 and A-F, about 16.7 million possibilities. The public 'which gym is this code' check answers any code, with no limit on how many tries one caller makes. A script that tries codes finds real gyms and gets their name and logo; with the code it can then join the gym as an app member under any name and read the gym's messages, offers and shop.
expected: Codes that cannot be found by trying: a limit on wrong codes per caller, or longer codes, so only people who saw the code at the gym can use it.
how_often: only when someone runs a script
fix_line: Count wrong codes per caller and stop after a few, or make new codes longer

title: Anyone can store any number of pictures on our server for free through a demo gym
what: 'Start demo' hands an owner key to anyone, with no sign-up. That key gets photo upload tickets, up to 50 at once. A ticket is not used up by an upload: for 15 minutes it lets in any number of files of up to 3 MB into a public picture store, and only the declared file type is checked. Files that no product or logo points at are never deleted. So a stranger can use our picture store as free public hosting, and we pay for the space.
expected: One upload per ticket (or a small number), and unused uploads cleaned away, so the picture store only holds pictures gyms really use.
fix_line: Make a ticket good for one file and delete pictures nothing points at

title: One person can block 'Start demo' for everyone, or block a gym's members from joining, for an hour
what: 'Start demo' stops after 300 demo gyms in an hour counted over all callers together, with no limit per caller, so one script can make 300 gyms and every real visitor then gets 'busy' for the rest of the hour. Joining a gym stops after 500 joins in an hour per gym, so anyone who has a gym's code can use that up and real members cannot join for an hour. The old 'create gym' for signed-in app users has no limit at all.
expected: Limits counted per caller, so one person cannot use up a shared allowance and lock out everybody else.
who: new owners trying the demo, members joining
fix_line: Add a per-caller limit before the shared one, and cap or retire the old create gym

items.reason: 168 functions listed. Every helper (name starting _) and every hq_ function plus support_make_signin_code is granted to the server role only. The gym and member functions open to the app roles each check a key first (owner key or session of any staff role; owner-only where desk is refused; or a member key), and every row they touch is filtered to that key's gym (for branches: the business's own gym list). With no key at all: demo_start_gym, gym_preview, member_join, app_limits, auth_gym_id, auth_role, _photo_ticket_ok (used by the storage rule). Signed-in only: create_gym, join_gym_by_code, delete_my_cloud_data and member_copy_* (own user id). Could not check: default PUBLIC execute rights do not show in the grant list and the definer settings query was not run; each file revokes PUBLIC by hand.

35 area tables, all with row rules on; only gyms (own gym), member_summary, profiles and member_items (own row) have a rule, the other 31 have none, so apps reach them only through the key-checked functions. Test proving gym B is refused with gym A's data present: crm_records, gym_members, gym_staff, gym_sessions, gym_owner_keys, gym_signin_codes, shop_orders, shop_products, gym_messages, gym_message_seen, gyms, receipt_history, gym_creator_ips, member_summary, profiles (uat_access_matrix: every gym B cell must be a refusal); gym_offers, offer_members (0025); gym_auto_reminders (0029); member_items (0032); gym_groups open-branch (0031); QR check-in roster (0015). A signed-in member who has the code can read the gym row (plan, paid-until, status): allowed on purpose by the matrix.

Only the all-tables loop, run while these tables are empty, covers gym_signin_fails, crm_push_log, member_checkin_tries, gym_checkin_misses, photo_tickets, branch_lookups, gym_message_to, offer_days, offer_log, gym_access_log and the hq_ tables (same cause: reused FN-L3-server-hq-gate-workers-04). The catalog shows row rules on with no rule, so apps cannot read them today. Terms acceptance: reused FN-L3-panel-auth-data-03. Branch visitor look-ups by another business: reused FN-L3-panel-pay-machines-01. app_config holds no gym data.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt, no live endpoint and no database function was called; everything is from code, tests and the catalog file.

All 32 key-pattern hits are the word service_role in comments or grant lines, not keys. No key, token or password is written in these files; the only fixed address is the public project address in the photo-link check, which is not secret. No APK code in this area.

No AI or outside-service key in this area. Gym keys, sessions, member keys and sign-in codes are random and stored only as a sha256 fingerprint, never in plain text; the key tables are closed to apps.

Session expiry: a session lives until signed out, and old owner keys and member keys never expire (reused FN-L3-panel-auth-data-01). Sign-in brute force: a 6-digit code lasts 30 minutes, 5 wrong tries per number and address and 50 per number in 30 minutes, about 1 in 20,000 per code: fine. The address limit reads the caller address header, which the proxy hides (reused FN-L3-server-panel-worker-01). PIN and PIN reset come in 0034, outside this area. The advisor says leaked-password protection is off for Supabase sign-in accounts: a project setting, noted only.

Every function passes typed text as values, never as SQL. The one built query (HQ delete proof) only inserts table names read from the catalog, safely quoted. Typed names are trimmed and cut to 60 characters, mobiles to digits, colours must match #RRGGBB, records are capped at 20,000 bytes and checked by kind. How the panel or app shows stored text is judged in those areas.

Product photo and logo uploads need a 15-minute ticket from an owner (desk refused); JPEG, PNG or WebP only, 3 MB or 1 MB, and a product or gym can only point at a file in its bucket. But a ticket takes any number of files, anyone gets an owner key from Start demo, and unused files are never deleted (finding). A gym pointing at another gym's public picture is harmless.

/j/<code> links use the 6-character join code, which can be found by trying with no limit (finding); the answer holds only name, colours and logo. The gym web pages come in later migrations, outside this area.
This area is database change files only; no npm or Gradle package is installed here. Dependency CVEs are judged in the app and Worker areas.
